questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Interpret the slope and the intercept of a linear model in the context of the data
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: ŷ = 4x + 58 predicts a test score from x hours of study. Interpret the slope and the intercept.
questions.prompt_markup:
ŷ = 4x + 58 predicts a test score from x hours of study.
Interpret the slope and the intercept.
questions.correct_answer: Slope: each additional hour of study goes with about 4 more points (predicted). Intercept: the predicted score for 0 hours is 58.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both interpretations, in context.

questions.skill: Interpret the slope and the intercept of a linear model in the context of the data
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A model for used cars is ŷ = 22,000 - 1,800x, where x is the age in years and ŷ is the price in dollars. Interpret -1,800 and 22,000.
questions.prompt_markup:
A model for used cars is ŷ = 22,000 - 1,800x, where x is the age in years and ŷ is the price in dollars.
Interpret -1,800 and 22,000.
questions.correct_answer: The predicted price drops about $1,800 for each year of age; the predicted price of a new (0-year-old) car is $22,000.

questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: ŷ = 0.9x - 20 predicts an adult's weight in pounds from height in inches. Does the intercept make sense in context? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
ŷ = 0.9x - 20 predicts an adult's weight in pounds from height in inches.
Does the intercept make sense in context? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. It predicts -20 pounds at a height of 0 inches, which is impossible and far outside the data.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the answer and the reason.

questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A(t) = 500e^(0.04t). What does 0.04 mean? When does A double, to the nearest tenth?
questions.prompt_markup:
A(t) = 500e^(0.04t).
What does 0.04 mean? When does A double, to the nearest tenth?
questions.correct_answer: A continuous growth rate of 4% per unit of t; t ≈ 17.3
questions.grading_note: Form required: the meaning and the rounded time. t = ln 2 ÷ 0.04.
